quotes.text: Was mich nicht umbringt, macht mich stärker.
quotes.translation: What does not kill me makes me stronger.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.notes: Often misattributed or quoted out of context. Part of Nietzsche's affirmation of life.

quotes.text: Ἓν οἶδα ὅτι οὐδὲν οἶδα.
quotes.translation: I know that I know nothing.
quotes.author: Socrates
quotes.notes: The Socratic paradox. Knowledge begins with recognizing ignorance.

quotes.text: L'enfer, c'est les autres.
quotes.translation: Hell is other people.
quotes.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
quotes.notes: Often misunderstood. Sartre meant that we see ourselves through others' judgments.

quotes.text: Il faut imaginer Sisyphe heureux.
quotes.translation: One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.notes: The conclusion of Camus's essay on the absurd.

quotes.text: Homo sum, humani nihil a me alienum puto.
quotes.translation: I am human, and I think nothing human is alien to me.
quotes.author: Terence
quotes.notes: A foundational statement of humanist ethics.

quotes.text: Wovon man nicht sprechen kann, darüber muß man schweigen.
quotes.translation: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
quotes.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
quotes.notes: The famous closing proposition of the Tractatus.

quotes.text: 知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也。
quotes.translation: To know what you know and what you do not know, that is true knowledge.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.notes: Epistemological humility in Confucian thought.

quotes.text: 道可道，非常道。名可名，非常名。
quotes.translation: The Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao. The name that can be named is not the eternal name.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.notes: The opening lines of the Dao De Jing.

quotes.text: Tudo vale a pena / Se a alma não é pequena.
quotes.translation: All is worthwhile / If the soul is not small.
quotes.author: Fernando Pessoa
quotes.notes: From the poem celebrating Portuguese maritime exploration.

quotes.text: O poeta é um fingidor. / Finge tão completamente / Que chega a fingir que é dor / A dor que deveras sente.
quotes.translation: The poet is a feigner. / He feigns so completely / That he even feigns as pain / The pain he truly feels.
quotes.author: Fernando Pessoa
quotes.notes: Pessoa's reflection on the nature of poetic creation.

quotes.text: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita / mi ritrovai per una selva oscura.
quotes.translation: Midway upon the journey of our life / I found myself within a forest dark.
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri
quotes.notes: The opening lines of the Commedia. Dante was 35, midway through the biblical lifespan.

quotes.text: Se vogliamo che tutto rimanga come è, bisogna che tutto cambi.
quotes.translation: If we want things to stay as they are, things will have to change.
quotes.author: Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa
quotes.notes: The quintessential expression of gattopardismo.

quotes.text: Fiat justitia, et pereat mundus.
quotes.translation: Let justice be done, though the world perish.
quotes.author: Ferdinand I
quotes.notes: Later criticized by Kant for its extremism.

quotes.text: Quis custodiet ipsos custodes?
quotes.translation: Who will guard the guards themselves?
quotes.author: Juvenal
quotes.notes: A perennial question of political philosophy.

quotes.text: 色即是空，空即是色。
quotes.translation: Form is emptiness, emptiness is form.
quotes.author: Heart Sutra
quotes.notes: Central teaching of Mahayana Buddhism.

quotes.text: 散る桜 残る桜も 散る桜
quotes.translation: Falling cherry blossoms — / even the remaining ones / will fall.
quotes.author: Ryokan
quotes.notes: A haiku embodying mono no aware.

quotes.text: Die Welt ist alles, was der Fall ist.
quotes.translation: The world is all that is the case.
quotes.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
quotes.notes: The opening proposition of the Tractatus.

quotes.text: Gott ist tot.
quotes.translation: God is dead.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.notes: Not a celebration but a diagnosis of modern nihilism.

quotes.text: L'homme est condamné à être libre.
quotes.translation: Man is condemned to be free.
quotes.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
quotes.notes: Freedom is not a gift but a burden we cannot escape.

quotes.text: Je pense, donc je suis.
quotes.translation: I think, therefore I am.
quotes.author: René Descartes
quotes.notes: The French formulation of the cogito.

quotes.text: Μηδὲν ἄγαν.
quotes.translation: Nothing in excess.
quotes.author: Delphic maxim
quotes.notes: One of the three Delphic maxims, along with 'Know thyself.'

quotes.text: Γνῶθι σεαυτόν.
quotes.translation: Know thyself.
quotes.author: Delphic maxim
quotes.notes: The most famous of the Delphic maxims.

quotes.text: Odi et amo. Quare id faciam, fortasse requiris. / Nescio, sed fieri sentio et excrucior.
quotes.translation: I hate and I love. Why do I do this, perhaps you ask. / I do not know, but I feel it happening and I am tormented.
quotes.author: Catullus
quotes.notes: The entire poem consists of this couplet.

quotes.text: Ars longa, vita brevis.
quotes.translation: Art is long, life is short.
quotes.author: Hippocrates
quotes.notes: Originally about medical knowledge. Latin translation of the Greek.

quotes.text: 人生得意須盡歡，莫使金樽空對月。
quotes.translation: When life fulfills your wishes, enjoy fully; / Do not let the golden cup face the moon empty.
quotes.author: Li Bai
quotes.notes: From one of the most celebrated Tang dynasty poems.

quotes.text: 祇園精舎の鐘の声、諸行無常の響きあり。
quotes.translation: The sound of the Gion temple bells echoes the impermanence of all things.
quotes.author: Anonymous
quotes.notes: The famous opening of the Tale of the Heike.

quotes.text: As armas e os barões assinalados / Que, da Ocidental praia Lusitana, / Por mares nunca de antes navegados / Passaram ainda além da Taprobana.
quotes.translation: Arms and the men distinguished / Who from the western Lusitanian shore / Through seas never before sailed / Passed even beyond Taprobana.
quotes.author: Luís de Camões
quotes.notes: The opening stanza of Portugal's national epic.

quotes.text: Ελευθερία ή θάνατος!
quotes.translation: Freedom or death!
quotes.author: Greek revolutionary motto
quotes.notes: The rallying cry of the Greek War of Independence.

quotes.text: La beauté sera CONVULSIVE ou ne sera pas.
quotes.translation: Beauty will be CONVULSIVE or will not be at all.
quotes.author: André Breton
quotes.notes: The closing line of Breton's surrealist novel.

quotes.text: Ich bin ein Berliner.
quotes.translation: I am a Berliner.
quotes.author: John F. Kennedy
quotes.notes: Expressing solidarity with West Berlin during the Cold War.

quotes.text: Der Mensch kann tun was er will; er kann aber nicht wollen was er will.
quotes.translation: Man can do what he wills but he cannot will what he wills.
quotes.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
quotes.source: Über die Freiheit des menschlichen Willens
quotes.notes: Schopenhauer's formulation of the problem of free will.

quotes.text: Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom.
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.notes: Kierkegaard's analysis of anxiety as fundamental to human existence.

quotes.text: Der Mensch ist nur da ganz Mensch, wo er spielt.
quotes.translation: Man is only fully human when he plays.
quotes.author: Friedrich Schiller
quotes.source: Über die ästhetische Erziehung des Menschen
quotes.notes: From Schiller's Letters on the Aesthetic Education of Man.

quotes.text: Slave morality from the outset says No to what is 'outside,' what is 'different,' what is 'not itself.'
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.notes: Nietzsche's analysis of the reactive nature of slave morality.

quotes.text: Ennui est entré dans les âmes comme une pluie dans le foin.
quotes.translation: Ennui has entered souls like rain into hay.
quotes.author: Gustave Flaubert
quotes.notes: From Flaubert's correspondence.

quotes.text: The crowd is his element, as the air is that of birds and water of fishes.
quotes.author: Charles Baudelaire
quotes.notes: Baudelaire's description of the flâneur's habitat.

quotes.text: ὕβρις φυτεύει τύραννον.
quotes.translation: Hubris plants the tyrant.
quotes.author: Sophocles
quotes.notes: From the choral ode, line 872.

quotes.text: Tragedy is an imitation of an action that is serious, complete, and of a certain magnitude.
quotes.author: Aristotle
quotes.notes: Aristotle's definition of tragedy.

quotes.text: War is a violent teacher.
quotes.author: Thucydides
quotes.source: History of the Peloponnesian War, III.82
quotes.notes: From Thucydides' analysis of civil strife in Corcyra.

quotes.text: In the tea-room it is left for each guest in imagination to complete the total effect in relation to himself.
quotes.author: Kakuzo Okakura
quotes.notes: Okakura's explanation of aesthetic incompleteness.

quotes.text: 物の哀れを知る — to know the pathos of things.
quotes.author: Motoori Norinaga
quotes.notes: Norinaga's formulation of the central Japanese aesthetic concept.

quotes.text: Tu regere imperio populos, Romane, memento.
quotes.translation: Remember, Roman, to rule the peoples with your power.
quotes.author: Virgil
quotes.notes: Anchises' prophecy of Rome's destiny.

quotes.text: Omnia, Lucili, aliena sunt, tempus tantum nostrum est.
quotes.translation: All things, Lucilius, are not ours; only time is our own.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.notes: Opening of Seneca's letters to Lucilius.

quotes.text: When an opponent declares, 'I will not come over to your side,' I calmly say, 'Your child belongs to us already.'
quotes.author: Adolf Hitler
quotes.notes: On the Nazi project of total coordination.

quotes.text: Wie Siegfried von dem hinterhältigen Speerwurf des grimmen Hagen getroffen, so stürzte unsere ermattete Front.
quotes.translation: As Siegfried was struck by the treacherous spear-throw of the grim Hagen, so collapsed our exhausted front.
quotes.author: Paul von Hindenburg
quotes.notes: Hindenburg's testimony that crystallized the stab-in-the-back myth.

quotes.text: Le terroir, c'est la mémoire de la terre.
quotes.translation: Terroir is the memory of the earth.
quotes.author: French viticulture tradition
quotes.notes: Attributed saying in French viticulture.

quotes.text: Noblesse oblige, ou : qui trop s'excuse, s'accuse.
quotes.translation: Nobility obliges, or: who excuses himself too much, accuses himself.
quotes.author: Gaston de Lévis
quotes.notes: The origin of the phrase 'noblesse oblige.'

quotes.text: Ex nihilo nihil fit.
quotes.translation: Nothing comes from nothing.
quotes.author: Lucretius
quotes.notes: The Epicurean principle against creation from nothing.

quotes.text: Dixitque Deus: Fiat lux. Et facta est lux.
quotes.translation: And God said: Let there be light. And there was light.
quotes.author: Vulgate
quotes.notes: The first divine speech act in the Bible.

quotes.text: ἦθος ἀνθρώπωι δαίμων.
quotes.translation: Character is fate for man.
quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.notes: Heraclitus' famous fragment on character and destiny.

quotes.text: El duende no llega si no ve la posibilidad de la muerte.
quotes.translation: The duende does not come if it does not see the possibility of death.
quotes.author: Federico García Lorca
quotes.notes: From Lorca's lecture on the dark spirit of art.

quotes.text: Caminante, son tus huellas el camino y nada más.
quotes.translation: Wanderer, your footsteps are the path and nothing more.
quotes.author: Antonio Machado
quotes.notes: From Machado's Proverbs and Songs.

quotes.text: No single word in English renders all the shades of toska.
quotes.author: Vladimir Nabokov
quotes.notes: Nabokov's definition of toska's untranslatability.

quotes.text: Saudade: um bem que se padece e um mal de que se goza.
quotes.translation: Saudade: a good that one suffers and an ill that one enjoys.
quotes.author: D. Francisco Manuel de Melo
quotes.notes: Classic Portuguese definition of saudade.
